title: Original Sin
definition: Original Sin is the inherited guilt and corruption connected to humanity’s fall in Adam.
summary: Original Sin is the inherited guilt and corruption connected to humanity’s fall in Adam.
christFocus: Christ is the last Adam who brings righteousness and life where Adam brought sin and death.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Original Sin teaches that we are not sinners merely because we sin; we sin because sin has touched the root of humanity in Adam. Scripture tells the truth about humanity without denying dignity and without minimizing the ruin sin has brought.

God gives this truth so people may stop hiding and come into the light. People who think they only need better habits miss the deeper need for rescue, new birth, and a better representative. The Bible’s honesty is mercy because what remains hidden cannot be healed rightly.

Christ enters the truth this doctrine exposes. Christ is the last Adam who brings righteousness and life where Adam brought sin and death. In Him, sinners are not left under guilt, shame, bondage, fear, or death; they are called to repentance, faith, restoration, and new life by the power of the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People need this truth because sin, shame, weakness, and brokenness are not solved by denial. People who think they only need better habits miss the deeper need for rescue, new birth, and a better representative. Scripture tells the truth so that people may stop hiding and come to Christ.

It also protects believers from shallow answers. Humanity needs forgiveness, new birth, restoration, and Spirit-empowered obedience, not merely better circumstances or stronger willpower.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look to Christ for a new standing and new life, not merely a better record. Bring this doctrine into prayer, Scripture, and daily obedience. Ask the Holy Spirit to make the truth real in your thinking, desires, relationships, and next faithful step with Christ.
